advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the install-certbot-timer.sh invocation in a `timeout` (as fetch/health/prune already are) so a hung certbot/dnf cannot hold the deploy lock.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:235: `elif ! bash "$MIRROR_DIR/infra/scripts/install-certbot-timer.sh"; then` — no `timeout` wrapper
install-certbot-timer.sh:53-57: `certbot certonly --webroot ... --non-interactive` (network op to Let's Encrypt, no local time bound)
install-certbot-timer.sh:32: `command -v nginx >/dev/null 2>&1 || dnf install -y nginx` and :39 `dnf install -y certbot ...`
autodeploy.sh:49: `FETCH_TIMEOUT="${FETCH_TIMEOUT:-60}"  # a hung fetch must not hold the lock` — the script's own stated invariant, which this unbounded block violates
autodeploy.sh:77-78: the block runs inside `exec 9>"$LOCK"` / `flock -n 9`, so a hang blocks every subsequent deploy
advisory.finding: The certbot re-materialize block invokes install-certbot-timer.sh with no timeout, but that installer performs unbounded blocking operations (certbot certonly network call to Let's Encrypt, dnf install, nginx reload) while holding the singleton deploy flock — a hang wedges all future autodeploy runs.

test_autodeploy_materialize_certbot.py:115-124 asserts only `marker.exists()` (installer ran) on the success path; test_...:127-135 asserts `not marker.exists()` on an unrelated diff — neither installs a failing installer stub nor asserts stdout/stderr for the `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR certbot-materialize-failed` marker
ABSENCE: no test seeds `install-certbot-timer.sh` to exit non-zero and then asserts (a) the AUTODEPLOY_ERROR marker is emitted on stderr and (b) the process still exits 0 / advances deployed-sha
advisory.finding: The certbot re-materialize block's distinct non-fatal-failure contract is untested: when `git checkout` or `install-certbot-timer.sh` fails the block must emit an `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR certbot-materialize-failed` marker AND continue (deploy advances the SHA, no rollback/abort), unlike the BOT_PATHS block which calls record_backoff_failure + exit 1. Neither new test drives the installer/checkout to fail, so a regression that makes this branch fatal or drops the error marker would pass both tests.
scenarios: A future refactor adds `exit 1`/`record_backoff_failure` to the certbot failure branch, breaking the non-fatal contract; both existing tests still pass.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the certbot re-materialize block's true blast radius (dnf install + Let's Encrypt ACME issuance + nginx reload) is acceptable in the unattended autodeploy path, or split the installer into a lightweight unit-file-only refresh mirroring install-observability.sh.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:225 comment: 'install-certbot-timer.sh is idempotent + runs as root (rewrites the unit files, daemon-reload; certbot no-ops when the cert is current)'
install-certbot-timer.sh:32 `command -v nginx >/dev/null 2>&1 || dnf install -y nginx`
install-certbot-timer.sh:33 `systemctl enable --now nginx`
install-certbot-timer.sh:53-57 `certbot certonly --webroot -w ... -d ${DOMAIN} --non-interactive --agree-tos -m ${EMAIL} --keep-until-expiring`
install-certbot-timer.sh:90 `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`
By contrast install-observability.sh:12-39 only `install`s one file and writes unit files (no package install, no network issuance, no service reload of a proxy fronting the gate).
install-certbot-timer.sh:53-57 unconditionally runs `certbot certonly ... --keep-until-expiring` on every invocation
autodeploy.sh:231-236 re-runs the installer whenever install-certbot-timer.sh changed between deployed..target
autodeploy.sh:225 comment only accounts for the current-cert no-op case ('certbot no-ops when the cert is current'), not the near-expiry / prior-failure case
autodeploy.sh:227 comment: 'DOMAIN/EMAIL flow through from the /etc/rebar/autodeploy.env sourced above, exactly as the installer's defaults expect'
autodeploy.sh:35 `[ -f /etc/rebar/autodeploy.env ] && . /etc/rebar/autodeploy.env` — the env file is not committed and no DOMAIN/EMAIL default is set in autodeploy.sh
install-certbot-timer.sh:27-28 `DOMAIN="${1:-${DOMAIN:-rebar.solutions.navateam.com}}"` / `EMAIL="${2:-${EMAIL:-joeoakhart@navapbc.com}}"` — hardcoded fallbacks
search_files for DOMAIN shows no assignment in autodeploy.sh or an env file; only docs and the installer/observability defaults
advisory.finding: The certbot re-materialize block re-runs install-certbot-timer.sh, which is NOT a lightweight timer refresh like the OBS sibling: it runs `dnf install` (nginx/certbot), `systemctl enable --now nginx`, a network-facing Let's Encrypt ACME issuance (`certbot certonly -d ${DOMAIN}`), and `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx` on the live fail-closed-gate box on every certbot-source change — a much larger blast radius than the comment's 'rewrites the unit files, daemon-reload' claim.
merged_from: The certbot re-materialize invokes `certbot certonly` against Let's Encrypt on every certbot-source change, exposing the box to ACME rate limits; the `--keep-until-expiring` no-op only applies while the cert is current, so a source change landing near expiry or after a failed prior validation can drive repeated live ACME attempts.

The comment claims 'DOMAIN/EMAIL flow through from the /etc/rebar/autodeploy.env sourced above,' but DOMAIN/EMAIL are not set anywhere in autodeploy.sh nor in any committed autodeploy.env — so the re-materialize actually falls back to the installer's hardcoded defaults, and a box originally installed with an overridden DOMAIN would silently converge to the wrong domain on re-materialize.
scenarios: A cosmetic edit to install-certbot-timer.sh lands on main; autodeploy re-runs the full installer, reloading host nginx (which fronts both gerrit and review-bot) on the live box.
dnf transient failure or a broken nginx config test during the unattended re-run leaves nginx in a degraded state on the gate host.
